newsitem.title: GERMANY: Electronic cash not a policy problem so far-Buba.
newsitem.headline: Electronic cash not a policy problem so far-Buba.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Tuesday that the increased use of various forms of electronic money had not so far presented a problem for its conduct of monetary policy.

In a report on innovations in payment systems in its March monthly report, the central bank said, "Overall, the Bundesbank can take a relaxed view of the newer developments in payment systems. These are not calling into question the bank's monopoly control of central bank money or demand for central bank money."
"Even control of the money supply has so far not come into serious difficulties as a result of these innovations," it added.
The Bundesbank said it did not expect this position to change in the foreseeable future, but added that it would continue to observe developments.

"Unexpected developments cannot be completely ruled out and it therefore seems appropriate to the Bundesbank to continue to take the entire monetary policy environment into account, alongside the money supply, when deciding policy," it said.
